# Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy

I'd learn to do inner-child therapy sober first, in your ordinary mindstate, since that's the one you'll be living in. Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis can help with that from the start, like I said about the urge to escape. When you’re ready, my [self-hypnosis guide](http://hypnosis.u-dont-exist.com/) or [lucid-dreaming guide](http://lucid.u-dont-exist.com/) can take it deeper. Low doses of entheogens can also synergize: cactus, CBD tea with sublingual mapacho, [Loveyhuasca](http://loveyhuasca.info/), [iboga](http://iboga.u-dont-exist.com/), and so on.

Remember those guards from the urge to escape? Same deal here. I'd want enough Nurturer and Protector around before you go deep, yours or borrowed from someone steady who won't try to take over the trip, and the caution signs from back there still count. But feeling attacked by a demon on a psychedelic is not necessarily paranoia. It can be real, and it's also not bad unless you're unprepared. It can be supremely empowering when you can send love and see how it fixes the situation.

Say a trip once showed you a love or a peace you never knew was possible. That matters, and it can stay a reference point, but there's no need to keep chasing it. Feeling it once on a psychedelic isn't the same as getting there without one, though. And getting back there in deep meditation now and then isn't the same as living from it on a random afternoon at work, which is kind of the whole point.

The beautiful state can become a hook, too. Say you had one amazing night on a psychedelic, or a dream like that, and now it's the bar, so regular life starts to feel like failing. How intense or beautiful it was doesn't prove that what you saw really happened, or that you're done healing. I'd look at what's changed once it wears off. Are you more honest, more protective of your little one, more reliable, all that?

And if your little one still can't take in the love, cranking up the intensity won't fix that, and neither will hunting for a bigger breakthrough. It's like yelling louder at someone who doesn't speak your language. Something's in the way, so find out what it is and meet that first. Maybe a protective part doesn't trust the love yet, or your little one learned long ago that love comes with strings attached.

## Altered States Can Require Reparenting

Have you ever been attacked by a literal demon? Maybe during sleep paralysis or meditation or on a psychedelic trip? A lot of modern folk laugh at this, yet it’s really quite a common experience. I was being psychically attacked by ghosts in my home as a child. Because I was literally a child, I was an easy target. And since most people never actually grew up, they are easy targets for every kind of influence, including spirit influence.

Those ghosts knew my weakness: dares. So they would dare me to jump out the window. I wasn’t suicidal, but I hated to seem like a “wussy.” Luckily, I trusted my parents with this information, and instead of taking me to a psychiatrist and pumping me full of anti-psychotic drugs, they put bars on the windows. Many kids are not so lucky in modern societies. They may get pumped full of anti-psychotic drugs for the rest of their life once diagnosed. That said, professional assessment may be warranted in some situations. I still played around with half-hanging out the windows, but I wasn’t quite dumb enough to jump out, and it meant something that my parents took it seriously.

As a semi-adult, age 26, I discovered meditation. After I began meditating deeply for a while, it seemed like my astral portal opened. I started getting attacked by spirits during sleep paralysis. They would sit on me, prevent me from breathing, and instill tremendous fear into the core of my being.

Yep. Exactly like that.

A trance like that can be "more scary" because you're trapped in it, but it's also less actually dangerous. You can't ruin your life at all in trance (unless a bad hypnotic suggestion gets deeply implanted, perhaps), while without trance you can "freak out" in a way that might end up getting you committed to a mental hospital, thrown out of your housing, going to jail, possibly even killing yourself. In trance you can basically work with the fear. You recognize it has no real world significance and it's purely just fear, so it's super useful that way.

After multiple episodes of this I decided to stop giving in to the victim mentality, and to start taking it seriously as a part of spiritual practice. My inner guide saw it as a perfect opportunity to demonstrate the power of love over fear. The next time it happened, despite how scary it was, I sent unconditional love to this demon on me. It took some minutes, but once that love was seen as enduring, the demon left, and it never returned.

I’ve also trained other people to do this during spiritual attack while on psychedelics. It works a lot better if you are already trained in [loving-kindness meditation](https://love.u-dont-exist.com/) to the point where it’s natural. I’d say it works way better than exorcism techniques (like [Julian Palmer’s torping](https://julianpalmerism.com/primer-malefic-entities/), which he also admits doesn’t work as well as love).

The astral plane is a bit different from the 3D. In the astral realm, unconditional love is a true, ultimately powerful physical force. Like a river, or a moat. There’s no evil that can trespass that moat. But don’t assume it will always work like that in the physical plane. It definitely has worked for me sometimes when facing some thugs, but [definitely not with others](https://defense.u-dont-exist.com/). Loving someone does not mean you leave the front door unlocked with a sign saying “take whatever you want.”

If you’re not able yet (or in the moment) to summon real love for an enemy, you can first send love to your frightened little one from your adult Nurturer. Many people also find they can borrow support from God, Jesus, angels, devas, or whatever loving spiritual presence fits their tradition. If I were to do that, I would still be framing it as “Please help this situation with love” rather than “Strike down the enemy!” But if a presence seems to enjoy your fear, it's not one of your grown-ups, borrowed or not, whatever it says it is. Same goes if it dares you to hurt or take advantage of anybody, yourself included.

It's basically borrowed adulthood. At first you may need to feel protected or loved by something bigger than you, before that love starts to feel like yours, and then bit by bit it becomes your own. Send some of it down to your frightened little one, and when that's possible, toward whatever you're afraid of. Continuing to relate to benevolent spiritual powers/beings is still perfectly fine, but they would surely be happy if they rubbed off on you!

If a voice or urge is directing you towards harm, and you feel at risk of acting on it, as with myself and those ghosts at home, move away from that open window and get some outside support. Know the limit of what you can handle, but don't turn it into a prison for life.

#### Non-altered states can feel like this too

Even if you’ve never literally been attacked by a demon that looked like the one above, the truth is that in this world, we’re always being manipulated and attacked by whatever evil force sees us as an easy target. Even social media algorithms will turn your life into hell if you don’t have the loving, protective inner parent developed. When you do, social media actually becomes useful and feels nice to interact with now and then.

Many people think reparenting sounds silly, or like the kind of ridiculous therapy people do when they have too much time or money. But you know what’s even sillier? Wandering the world aimlessly and getting manipulated by all kinds of evil forces. 💀

## How This Relates to IFS

If you know Internal Family Systems (IFS), a lot of this will look familiar. IFS recognizes protective parts too, and teaches people to approach them without shame or a fight, so meeting the protector first fits right in. My reparenting method diverges from IFS at an important point. In standard IFS, the healer is the Self, a calm, compassionate source inside you that's supposed to show up once your parts "unblend." I emphasize the inner adult you build and practice occupying: Nurturer, Protector, and Leader, Guide, or Guru.

Borrowed adulthood makes the difference even clearer. If that calm inner source just isn't there for you, borrow one grown-up job at a time and take it in gradually. It might come from a relationship, or an image, or a plan, whatever works. I have no use for another neo-Advaita, [spiritual-bypassing](http://goenka.u-dont-exist.com/) claim that a perfect Higher Self is already waiting underneath everything. The grown-up you can trust is something you build, by caring for yourself and holding boundaries, and by actually doing things and choosing where you're headed.

IFS calls these wounded young parts "exiles." I find that pathologizing. I prefer to speak of a child who needs parenting and integration, rather than naming them by their wounded or excluded condition. IFS "unburdening," often done after witnessing a part's origin story, can be powerful. But it can also get dramatic, with a lot of focus on memories and plenty of room for suggestion, and that can knock people off balance, especially if they tend to dissociate (DID-like fragmentation included) or to spiritually bypass.

And the map keeps growing: managers, firefighters, exiles, polarized parts, legacy burdens, Self-energy, guides, new subparts and so on, until it can turn into a maze. Some practitioners use the model gently. Others seem to deepen the fragmentation while they're trying to resolve it. A framework with institutes and certifications behind it isn't automatically more true, or safer for that matter.

A good IFS therapist may still help. Look for a grounded, trauma-informed one who doesn't steer you toward answers, especially someone who really understands dissociation. But if it's inner-child pain you're dealing with (shame, say, or a habit of abandoning yourself), a good reparenting therapist may fit better, and the same goes if there's no reliable grown-up in there yet. Either way, it's worth knowing the strengths and pitfalls of both before you pick.

### Related Clinical Work

This framework grew out of my own practice, plus the teachers and collaborators I credit below. Later revisions also compare notes with other approaches, like schema therapy, compassion-focused therapy, attachment repair, motivational interviewing, mentalizing, metacognitive therapy, behavioral activation, radically open DBT, emotion-focused therapy, spiritually integrated psychotherapy and so on. They don't all claim the same things. I borrow particular distinctions and practices from them, and I'm not saying they'd agree with the whole synthesis, or that their research backs it up as a package.

## Teachers and Practice Resources

Several teachers directly influenced this method. I can’t fully endorse any of them because none follows my whole approach or has expressed interest in doing so. Daja works with inner-child pl/ork intuitively, through the divine Nurturer and Protector archetypes. It's less neuroscience and CBT and more direct archetypal practice, and the three grown-up jobs draw a lot from it. She has a [book](https://a.co/d/7Sa4kP2) and a [free one-hour YouTube training](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL_kbcFWhZK0wJeFUShGvHFZa1u3x7p8Y-&si=Fr0g76mDh8-WLMjM), and she's on [Instagram](http://instagram.com/ihopeyoufindserenity). I also made a [Gemini thread](https://g.co/gemini/share/fe062bfb8847) that turns her training into an interactive tool.

Lisa Romano brings more neuroscience and CBT, and her [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2tbMRZKdHJ4) is a good place to start. She makes the point that remembering the specific details of childhood trauma isn't necessary, because the felt body knows what needs to come up. Key, who I mentioned earlier for the Guide and the identity work, led a [guided inner-child meditation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UkVlDixqqA0) for twenty people in Nairobi in January 2026, and it's up on YouTube.

If you're looking for a therapist, [Open Path Collective](https://openpathcollective.org/pricing-and-eligibility-for-affordable-therapy/) lists thousands of affordable ones. Filter for Internal Family Systems, since IFS-trained therapists often have the most relevant background for inner-child pl/ork. And for bottom-up support, there's my [Somatic Therapies Guide](http://somatic.u-dont-exist.com/).
